ram_model: Heap-only, no static buffers (data=0, bss=0). trex_compile does 4 mallocs: struct TRex 52 B, node array strlen(pattern)*16 B grown by realloc doubling (node = 16 B: type,left,right,next ints), jmp_buf 92 B (newlib ARM), match table (ngroups+1)*8 B. Compile-time recursion: trex_element recurses once per SEQUENTIAL element (trex.c:313) and trex_list once per alternative -> stack depth O(pattern length) (24 B frame each per -fstack-usage, plus call overhead); parse errors longjmp out. Match-time recursion: trex_matchnode (48 B frame) recurses per nested node / greedy look-ahead chain -> depth O(pattern nodes), NOT O(text length) (repetition is iterative). Quantifier bounds packed as two 16-bit fields (0xFFFF = unbounded). Char type is 8-bit char (or 16-bit with _UNICODE); MAX_CHAR+N opcode encoding.
features_verified: IMPLEMENTED (read from trex.c): literals; escapes \t \n \r \f \v and backslash-quoted metachar; '.' (matches ANY byte incl newline and the NUL terminator); ^ only at start of a branch (elsewhere literal); $ (OP_EOL); alternation | (no empty alternatives); capturing () and non-capturing (?:); greedy-syntax quantifiers * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} (bounds 16-bit); [classes] with ranges, negation [^, escapes and \d-style class escapes inside; predefined classes \a \A \w \W \s \S \d \D \x \X(hex digit) \c \C \p \P \l(lower) \u(upper) via ctype; \b \B (whitespace-based, off by one); trex_match (anchored whole-string), trex_search/trex_searchrange (search anywhere, scans start positions itself), trex_getsubexp (group 0 = whole match). NOT IMPLEMENTED: lazy quantifiers (a*? parses as a* followed by literal '?'); case-insensitive flag (no tolower/toupper anywhere); UTF-8 awareness (byte-wise; any byte >127 or <32 in a PATTERN is rejected by the isprint() gate 'letter expected', so non-ASCII literals/classes are impossible); empty pattern, empty alternative, anchor-only pattern (grammar demands >=1 element); literal '-' at class edge; possessive/atomic, backrefs, lookaround, named groups, \x hex escapes, \uXXXX; min>max in {n,m} undiagnosed. SEMANTICS: NOT a backtracking engine -- each quantifier stops at the first count >= min where the single following node matches, and alternation/quantifiers are never re-entered on later failure: 'a.*b' on 'axxbxxb' -> 0-4 (Perl 0-7), '(a|ab)c' on 'abc' -> nomatch, '(a+)(a)' on 'aaa' -> nomatch-ish (0-2). Capture bookkeeping is an ordinal counter (_currsubexp), so groups are lost ('(a*)(b)' group 2 unset, 'x(a)|(b)' group 2 unset), stale ('x(a)y|a' on 'xab' reports group 1) and repeated groups keep the FIRST iteration ('(ab)+' -> 0-2).

caveats: (1) T-Rex is NOT a backtracking matcher; its '*'/'+' are effectively shortest-match-then-commit, so it does not implement Perl/JS leftmost-first semantics even for ASCII-only patterns -- the 628 passes are mostly patterns where that difference is invisible. (2) Raw API is memory-unsafe: trex_compile('') writes through NULL/corrupts heap; matching reads past the NUL terminator (ASan-confirmed); unterminated '[' walks the pattern until the isprint gate stops it because _eol is NULL during compile. (3) 8-bit only; every byte >0x7F in a pattern is rejected, so UTF-8 literals cannot even be expressed; UTF-8 text is matched byte-wise. (4) Requires malloc/realloc/free and setjmp/longjmp (92 B jmp_buf on Cortex-M) -- violates the project's no-malloc requirement. (5) 2929 B Cortex-M4 (-Os, text incl. 195 B of error strings) is already above the 1000-2000 B target while lacking lazy quantifiers, case-insensitivity, UTF-8 and correct backtracking. (6) The Squirrel C++ port (sqstdrex.cpp, 3144 B with g++ -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti) adds eol checks in OP_DOT/OP_CLASS/OP_CCLASS (fixes the over-read) and an OP_MB 'match balanced' extension but shares the parser/matcher design and its semantics; measured as secondary only. (7) 'text' numbers are per measure.sh (section sums of the .o, no linking); the C++ number is not directly comparable (different language front-end, ctype as functions). (8) The Cortex-M0+ figure being smaller than M4 is expected here (fewer 32-bit Thumb-2 encodings emitted at -Os for this code).
